title: DC Sources & Circuits

notes.heading: 1. KCL, KVL, Superposition & Star-Delta (Y–Δ) Conversions
notes.proseLatex: Kirchhoff's Current Law ($\sum I = 0$ at a node) expresses charge conservation; Kirchhoff's Voltage Law ($\sum V = 0$ around a closed loop) expresses energy conservation. Superposition applies to voltages and currents in linear bilateral networks (deactivating independent voltage sources to SHORT circuits and independent current sources to OPEN circuits — NEVER deactivate dependent sources, and NEVER add component powers $I^2 R$ by superposition!). Equal resistors convert cleanly via $R_\Delta = 3 R_Y$.

keyFormulas.label: Current/Voltage Divider & Symmetric Y–Δ Rule
keyFormulas.latex: $I_1 = I\,\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2},\qquad V_1 = V\,\frac{R_1}{R_1 + R_2},\qquad R_\Delta = 3 R_Y\;\text{(symmetric)}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Apply current divider (opposite branch R in numerator!) and star-delta collapse.

notes.heading: 2. Thévenin, Norton & Maximum Power Transfer Theorem
notes.proseLatex: Any linear two-terminal network reduces to a Thévenin voltage $V_{\text{th}} = V_{\text{oc}}$ in series with $R_{\text{th}}$ (or Norton current $I_N = I_{\text{sc}} = V_{\text{th}}/R_{\text{th}}$ in parallel with $R_N = R_{\text{th}}$). A variable resistive load $R_L$ extracts MAXIMUM power when matched to the source resistance $R_L = R_{\text{th}}$, yielding $P_{\max} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4 R_{\text{th}}}$ at exactly $50\%$ efficiency! (Notice $50\%$ is efficiency AT maximum power transfer, NOT maximum efficiency — $\eta = \frac{R_L}{R_L + R_{\text{th}}} \to 100\%$ as $R_L \to \infty$!).

keyFormulas.label: Thévenin-Norton Duality & Maximum Power Transfer
keyFormulas.latex: $V_{\text{th}} = I_N R_{\text{th}},\qquad R_L = R_{\text{th}} \implies P_{\max} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4 R_{\text{th}}}\;(\eta = 50\%)$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute Vth, Rth, maximum load power, and distinguish max power from max efficiency.

examples.problemLatex: A linear DC network has open-circuit voltage $24\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $6\text{ A}$ at terminals $A$-$B$. Find $R_L$ for maximum power transfer and $P_{\max}$.

notes.heading: 3. First-Order RC & RL DC Transients & Steady-State Shortcuts
notes.proseLatex: Capacitor voltage $v_C(t)$ and inductor current $i_L(t)$ CANNOT jump instantaneously ($v_C(0^+) = v_C(0^-)$ and $i_L(0^+) = i_L(0^-)$). In DC steady state ($t \to \infty$), an ideal capacitor acts as an OPEN CIRCUIT and an ideal inductor acts as a SHORT CIRCUIT! Every first-order transient obeys $x(t) = x(\infty) + [x(0^+) - x(\infty)]e^{-t/\tau}$ with time constant $\tau_{RC} = R_{\text{th}} C$ and $\tau_{RL} = \frac{L}{R_{\text{th}}}$ (reaching $63.2\%$ of total change at $t = \tau$ and $>99\%$ by $5\tau$).

keyFormulas.label: Universal First-Order Step Response & Time Constants
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Evaluate t = 0+ continuity, t = infinity open/short equivalents, and RC/RL time constants.

workedExamples.problemLatex: A linear DC network has open-circuit voltage $24\text{ V}$ and short-circuit current $6\text{ A}$ at terminals $A$-$B$. Find $R_L$ for maximum power transfer and $P_{\max}$.
An uncharged $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is connected across $100\text{ V}$ DC through $R = 50\text{ k}\Omega$ at $t = 0$. Find time constant $\tau$ and $v_C(0.5\text{ s})$.

wbjeebTraps: Notice $\tau_{RC} = R\cdot C$ whereas $\tau_{RL} = L / R$ (do NOT write $L\cdot R$!).

Charging an uncharged capacitor $C$ from a constant DC source $V$ through ANY resistance $R$ stores $\frac{1}{2}CV^2$ in the capacitor and ALWAYS dissipates an equal $\frac{1}{2}CV^2$ as heat in $R$ (50% charging efficiency regardless of $R$!).
Superposition NEVER applies directly to power ($P = I^2 R$ is non-linear): compute net $I = I_1 + I_2$ FIRST, then square!

conceptPrimer.heading: KCL and KVL Are Conservation Laws
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Kirchhoff's Current Law $\sum I = 0$ at a node is charge conservation; Kirchhoff's Voltage Law $\sum V = 0$ around a loop is energy conservation. Every network method (mesh, nodal) is bookkeeping on these two. Micro-check: three currents meet at a node ($2\ \text{A}$ in, $3\ \text{A}$ in, $x$ out): $x = 5\ \text{A}$ — KCL.

conceptPrimer.heading: Superposition — With Its Two Red Lines
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: In linear bilateral networks, each independent source's contribution to any VOLTAGE or CURRENT can be computed alone: kill other ideal voltage sources (SHORT them) and ideal current sources (OPEN them). Never deactivate DEPENDENT sources. And superposition NEVER applies to power: $P = I^2R$ is nonlinear — add currents first, then square. Micro-check: two sources give $I_1 = 2\ \text{A}$, $I_2 = 3\ \text{A}$ through $R = 1\ \Omega$: net power uses $I = 5\ \text{A} \Rightarrow 25\ \text{W}$, not $4 + 9 = 13\ \text{W}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Dividers and the Symmetric Y–Δ Rule
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Current divider: the branch current carries the OPPOSITE resistance in the numerator, $I_1 = I\frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$; voltage divider keeps its own, $V_1 = V\frac{R_1}{R_1+R_2}$. For equal resistors, the conversion shortcut is $R_\Delta = 3R_Y$. Micro-check: $10\ \text{A}$ splits into $2\ \Omega$ and $8\ \Omega$: the $2\ \Omega$ branch carries $10 \times \frac{8}{10} = 8\ \text{A}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Thévenin and Norton: Two Faces of One Network
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Any linear two-terminal network reduces to an open-circuit voltage $V_{\text{th}} = V_{\text{oc}}$ in series with $R_{\text{th}}$, or a short-circuit current $I_N = I_{\text{sc}} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}}{R_{\text{th}}}$ in parallel with $R_N = R_{\text{th}}$. Measure $V_{\text{oc}}$ and $I_{\text{sc}}$ and you have both: $R_{\text{th}} = \frac{V_{\text{oc}}}{I_{\text{sc}}}$. Micro-check: $V_{\text{oc}} = 24\ \text{V}$, $I_{\text{sc}} = 6\ \text{A}$: $R_{\text{th}} = 4\ \Omega$, $I_N = 6\ \text{A}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Maximum Power Transfer — and Its 50% Catch
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: A variable resistive load extracts maximum power at $R_L = R_{\text{th}}$, delivering $P_{\max} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4R_{\text{th}}}$ — but at exactly $50\%$ efficiency, since the source resistance burns an equal share. $50\%$ is the efficiency AT maximum power, NOT the maximum efficiency ($\eta = \frac{R_L}{R_L + R_{\text{th}}} \to 100\%$ as $R_L \to \infty$). Micro-check: $V_{\text{th}} = 24\ \text{V}$, $R_{\text{th}} = 4\ \Omega$: $P_{\max} = \frac{576}{16} = 36\ \text{W}$, with $18\ \text{W}$ lost inside.

conceptPrimer.heading: Transients: Continuity, Steady State and the Universal Form
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Capacitor voltage and inductor current CANNOT jump: $v_C(0^+) = v_C(0^-)$, $i_L(0^+) = i_L(0^-)$. In DC steady state a capacitor is an OPEN circuit and an inductor a SHORT. Every first-order transient obeys $x(t) = x(\infty) + [x(0^+) - x(\infty)]e^{-t/\tau}$ with $\tau_{RC} = R_{\text{th}}C$, $\tau_{RL} = \frac{L}{R_{\text{th}}}$ — $63.2\%$ of the change at $t = \tau$, $>99\%$ by $5\tau$. Micro-check: $R = 50\ \text{k}\Omega$, $C = 10\ \mu\text{F}$: $\tau = 0.5\ \text{s}$, and at $0.5\ \text{s}$ a $100\ \text{V}$ charge has reached $63.2\ \text{V}$.

keyFormulas.label: Superposition power ban
keyFormulas.latex: $P \ne P_1 + P_2$; use net $I$ then square

keyDefinitions.definition: Node current sum zero (charge conservation) / loop voltage sum zero (energy conservation).
Network obeying superposition — same response for either current direction, linear elements.
Source whose value is controlled by another circuit variable; never deactivated in superposition.
Open-circuit voltage source in series with the killed-network resistance.
Short-circuit current source in parallel with $R_{\text{th}}$; the dual of Thévenin.
The time for $63.2\%$ of the total first-order change; $RC$ or $L/R$.
Capacitor $\to$ open circuit; inductor $\to$ short circuit, as $t \to \infty$.
The exponential transition between initial and final states, dead beyond $\approx 5\tau$.

memoryHooks: KCL counts charge; KVL counts energy.
Voltage source dies shorted; current source dies open; dependent sources never die.
Divider numerators: voltage keeps its own R, current takes the other.
Equal resistors: delta is thrice the star.
Match for power ($R_L = R_{\text{th}}$), mismatch for efficiency.
DC steady state: C open, L short.
commonMistakes: Shorting current sources or opening voltage sources when deactivating.
Using the same resistor in both divider numerators.
Calling 50% efficiency the maximum possible efficiency.
Treating a capacitor as short (or inductor as open) in DC steady state.
Forgetting $R_\Delta = 3R_Y$ holds only for EQUAL resistors.
examChecklist: Write KCL/KVL conservation meanings before solving.
Superposition: short $V$-sources, open $I$-sources, spare dependent ones.
Never superpose power; net current first, then $I^2R$.
Dividers: own-R for voltage, opposite-R for current.
State continuity of $v_C$, $i_L$ at $0^+$ before any transient.
DC steady state: capacitor open, inductor short.
Compute $\tau = R_{\text{th}}C$ or $L/R_{\text{th}}$; use the universal response.
